function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is any vpn is installed". They want to check if any VPN is installed. We need to use the cmd_controller_execute tool to run a command that checks for installed VPNs. On Windows, we can query installed programs via WMIC or PowerShell. For example, we can use wmic product where "name like '%VPN%'" get name. Or use Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product. But better to use PowerShell: Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Where-Object {$_.Name -like "*VPN*"} | Select-Object Name.

We can chain commands: 'powershell -Command "Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Where-Object {$_.Name -like '*VPN*'} | Select-Object Name"'. That will list installed products with "VPN" in name. Alternatively, use 'wmic product where "name like '%VPN%'" get name'.
